name: infoblox-hosts_get_host_config
description: Fetch the requested variant of the DNS or DHCP configuration files for a specific on-prem host. Returns the base configuration by default; pass `variant=dfp` to get the DNS Firewall Proxy configuration a NIOS-X host running DFP actually loads, or `variant=ibpolicy` when that host runs DFP together with the On-Prem Policy Engine. The response names the effective file and why it was chosen; for NIOS-X DNS `files` also carries any custom root hints files (`root.servers.*`) in the selected bundle version. Use to read how one specific host is configured: forwarders, recursion, DHCP pools, reservations, options, and DDNS behavior. The files are that host's effective runtime configuration, so names in them can differ from the names shown in the Portal (for example the default DNS view appears as `_default`). Not a source for listing, counting, or confirming the existence of DNS views, zones, or records across a grid or many hosts: use the Portal DNS configuration API (DnsConfig) for those, where NIOS grid objects appear with their Portal names. If you have no tool for that API, say so instead of answering from one host's files. For Microsoft DNS hosts the response carries a `collection` object; `files` is empty only when `collection.evidence_available` is `false`, because the evidence was withheld or never collected (see `collection.reason`), not because the host has no configuration. A `snapshot_stale` result is `degraded` but still carries the stale snapshot in `files` and its `version` (`evidence_available` is `true`); check `collection.freshness` before relying on it. Do not use for general explanations, runtime troubleshooting, or multi-host summaries.

name: infoblox-portal_search_available_services
description:
Search for Infoblox Portal API services relevant to the current task.

Returns a ranked list of services with their endpoints. Each response includes
next_steps guidance on how to proceed based on what was found.

Pass only the relevant HTTP methods to reduce endpoint noise for large services.
For example, pass `["GET"]` for read-only tasks, or `["POST"]` for create operations.

name: infoblox-portal_list_all_available_services
description:
List every Infoblox Portal API service with a short description. Returns names and
descriptions only, with no endpoints or methods.

Prefer search_available_services to find the service for a request. Use this tool
when that search returns no relevant match, or when it isn't available, to check
whether a service exists before concluding the request is unsupported.

name: infoblox-portal_get_service_info
description: Discover methods available for a service.

name: infoblox-portal_get_method_info
description:
Get detailed parameter requirements for a specific endpoint.

Call this ONLY in the following cases:
- POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE: always call before submitting the request.
- GET with requires_method_info=true: the endpoint has non-standard query parameters.

GET endpoints where requires_method_info=false use standard filter params, so you
usually don't need this: use filter_fields from the search result in the _filter query
param of make_get_request, following the _filter grammar in its description. Call this
only if a GET still fails with a filter error you can't resolve from that grammar.

name: infoblox-portal_make_get_request
description:
Execute a GET request to retrieve information and store it for later SQL querying.

The response data will be stored in a session-specific directory and can be queried
using the `query_stored_data` tool with SQL.

Filtering Strategy:
1. Server-side filtering: Use the _filter parameter in query_params for simple
    top-level field filtering. Example: {"_filter": "name == 'John'"}. IMPORTANT: The _filter
    parameter only supports basic expressions on top-level fields and does not handle nested fields.
    For example: {"_filter": "name == 'John' and age > 30"} is supported,
    but {"_filter": "user.name == 'John'"} is not supported.
    _filter grammar:
    - Operators: == != > >= < <= ~ (regex match) !~ (regex no-match) and or not.
    - No contains / startsWith / endsWith / like / in and no function calls. For a substring
      use ~: name ~ 'east' (prefix: name ~ '^east'). ~= is not an operator.
    - Quote every literal, booleans included: disabled == 'true'.
    - Use only fields listed in filter_fields.
    _order_by is 'field' or 'field desc' (comma-separated for several), never '-field' or 'field:desc'.

2. Client-side SQL queries: After calling this tool, use `query_stored_data` to run
    SQL queries against the stored data for:
    - Filtering on nested fields
    - Complex conditions (AND/OR)
    - Joins across multiple GET requests
    - Aggregations (COUNT, AVG, SUM, etc.)
    - Analysis of results

Inherited settings: in some APIs a resource inherits settings from other resources, so a stored
field may not be the value in effect. The service's description says how to read the value in
effect.

name: infoblox-portal_make_post_request
description:
Execute a POST request to create new objects or perform complex analysis.

Calling this tool will surface a UI confirmation form for the user with the ability
to edit fields before any changes are committed. Call this tool directly when the user asks to update
or modify something — you do not need to ask for permission or clarification first.

Any items in body or query_params will be pre-populated in the confirmation form shown to the user.
Always populate these arguments where possible, either from the user's request or best inference.

Writing a body:
- Don't copy fields the server sets, such as ids and timestamps, from a GET result into a body.
- When get_method_info returns `write_guidance` for the endpoint, follow it.
- If a result carries a `write_guards` list (how the body was adjusted to fit the API) or `no_change: true`, tell
  the user what was changed and why, in plain terms, without naming `write_guards`.

name: infoblox-portal_make_put_request
description:
Execute a PUT request to create or replace objects.

Calling this tool will surface a UI confirmation form for the user with the ability

Any items in body or query_params will be pre-populated in the confirmation form shown to the user.
Always populate these arguments where possible, either from the user's request or best inference.

Writing a body:

- If a result carries a `write_guards` list (how the body was adjusted to fit the API) or `no_change: true`, tell
  the user what was changed and why, in plain terms, without naming `write_guards`.
params: body:[{'additionalProperties': True, 'description': 'Body to include with the request', 'type': 'object'}, {'type': 'null'}]

name: infoblox-portal_make_patch_request

Execute a PATCH request to update existing objects.

Calling this tool will surface a UI confirmation form for the user with the ability

name: infoblox-portal_make_delete_request

Execute a DELETE request to remove objects.

Calling this tool will surface a UI confirmation form for the user with the ability

Any items in body or query_params will be pre-populated in the confirmation form shown to the user.

name: infoblox-portal_entity_search
description:
Find out what a name, identifier or indicator in the user's question refers to.

Use this first whenever a question names something whose type is not obvious,
rather than guessing which service or cube owns it. Four kinds of input:

- **An ambiguous noun.** "How many servers do we have" can mean `dhcp/server`
  or `dns/server`; "zones" spans auth, forward and stub. Returns every
  candidate entity type flagged `ambiguous` so the answer can name them or
  ask which was meant, instead of silently picking one.
- **A canonical identifier**, e.g. `dns/auth_zone/6b230bfc-...`. Returns the
  entity type it belongs to and marks the id opaque: pass it onward exactly
  as given, never rebuild it from the bare UUID.
- **An external indicator** — a domain, IP, URL, email or file hash. Looks it
  up in threat intelligence and returns the sources that had a finding,
  alongside a summary of everything checked.
- **A named object in the customer's own environment** (host, DNS record,
  asset, tag, user). Matched exactly through Global Search.

Also answers "how many actions/insights/alerts", broken down by severity and
status across both DDI and Threat Defense.

Not a web search: external indicators are looked up in Infoblox threat
intelligence, not on the open internet.

Returns a list of results, each tagged with the `mode` that produced it.

name: infoblox-portal_search_available_cubes
description:
Search for the most relevant CubeJS cubes using semantic similarity.

Use this tool to discover which cube contains the data you need. Returns
lightweight summaries (name, description, and field-name lists) for the
top matching cubes. The search index is built from each cube's name,
description, all measure names/descriptions, and all dimension
names/descriptions, so queries like 'bytes transferred by host' or
'query type breakdown' match on field-level concepts, not just titles.

name: infoblox-portal_list_all_cubes
description:
List all available CubeJS cubes and their descriptions.

Use this tool to discover what analytical data cubes are available.
Each cube represents a dataset that can be queried for insights.
Available cubes cover areas including: DNS (activity logs, metrics), DHCP (activity logs, metrics), Tokens (utilization only, capacity is in services), Insights/Actions (network, config, security, Infoblox IQ, assets), Assets (inventory, users, network interfaces, discovery provider details, insights).

When 5 or fewer cubes exist, full details (dimensions, measures, segments)
are automatically included. For more than 5 cubes, only summaries are
returned.

Returns a list of cubes with:
- name: The cube identifier to use in queries
- title: Human-readable name
- description: What data the cube contains
- type: Whether it's a 'cube' or 'view'
- dimensions, measures, segments: (only when <= 5 cubes)

name: infoblox-portal_get_cube_info
description:
Get detailed metadata for a specific CubeJS cube.

Returns comprehensive information about the cube including:
- Dimensions: Fields you can group by or filter on (e.g., device_ip, timestamp)
- Measures: Aggregatable values (e.g., count, sum, average)
- Segments: Pre-defined filters that can be applied

Example dimension types:
- string: Text values for filtering/grouping
- number: Numeric values
- time: Timestamps that support time-based analysis
- boolean: True/false values

Example measure types:
- count: Number of records
- sum: Total of numeric values
- avg: Average value
- min/max: Extreme values

name: infoblox-portal_query_cube
description:
Execute a CubeJS query and store results for SQL analysis.

Query Building Tips:
1. Always use fully qualified names (CubeName.field) for measures and dimensions
2. Time dimensions support relative ranges like '24 hours', '7 days' (auto-converted to date tuples)
3. Filters use operators like: equals, notEquals, contains, gt, gte, lt, lte

Common Patterns:
- Time series: Add time_dimensions with granularity for trends over time
- Top N: Use order with limit to get highest/lowest values
- Filtering: Use filters to narrow down to specific criteria
- Segments: Use segments for a cube's named, pre-defined filters (see get_cube_info)
- Grouping: Add dimensions to segment data by categories

name: infoblox-portal_query_stored_data
description:
Execute a SQL query against stored API response data using DuckDB.

This tool allows you to:
- Query data from previous GET requests using standard SQL
- Join data across multiple API responses
- Filter, aggregate, and analyze data with full SQL capabilities

Table naming: Tables are named based on the service, method, and endpoint.
Use the table_name returned from make_get_request (e.g., 'ipamsvc_get_ipam_subnet.parquet')
Query only table_names returned by other tool calls; cube names and endpoint names
are not tables. If a query names
a table that does not exist, the error lists the session's tables (available_tables).

DuckDB SQL Features:
- Standard SQL: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, etc.
- Aggregations: COUNT(), SUM(), AVG(), MIN(), MAX()
- Window functions, CTEs, and more

Examples:
- Simple query: "SELECT * FROM ipamsvc_get_ipam_subnet.parquet WHERE address LIKE '10.%'"
- Nested field filtering: "SELECT * FROM dns_get_records.parquet WHERE data.type = 'A'"
- Join: "SELECT a.*, b.name FROM table1.parquet a JOIN table2.parquet b ON a.id = b.id"
- Aggregate: "SELECT status, COUNT(*) as count FROM ipamsvc_get_ipam_subnet.parquet GROUP BY status"
- List tables: "SELECT * FROM _catalog" to see available session tables

name: infoblox-portal_get_approval_form
description: Return the A2UI form-group payload for a pending approval.

name: infoblox-portal_show_table
description:
This tool is used to present query results with zero transcription risk and with human-friendly rendering.
The assistant is responsible for preparing the dataset before calling this tool so the displayed table is
concise and readable.

Large results are fine: the user-facing table is paginated, so it is OK to display an arbitrarily large
stored table. Do not truncate, sample, or summarize rows just to keep the result short, and do not copy rows
into the chat. The table also supports built-in download to CSV and JSON, so there is no need to offer or
generate exports separately.

Hard requirements (MUST)
* User-ready table: The table shown must be ready for end-user consumption: clear column names,
    human-readable values, and no internal identifiers unless explicitly requested.
* Column limits: Prefer ≤ 5 columns. If more than 5 columns are relevant, the assistant MUST either:
    split into multiple tables, or summarize and show only the most important columns.
* No internal identifiers: Do not include id, uuid, ophid, opaque keys, or similar identifier columns unless the
    user explicitly asks.
* Dates: Display timestamps in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC (UTC-0) where applicable.
* Numeric formatting: Round floats to 2 decimals unless higher precision is required by the user's question.
    Use consistent units.
* Flattening: Nested objects must be flattened into columns. Lists should be joined into a single string with
    a delimiter (e.g., ", "), or summarized (e.g., "3 items") when very long.
* Semantic Value Humanization (required): Raw categorical/enum/boolean values MUST be rendered in a
    human-friendly form. The assistant MUST apply the following generic rules across all domains
    (DNS, DHCP, IPAM, security, assets, etc.):
    - Normalize first: trim whitespace, lowercase for matching, and treat _/- as word separators.
        Treat boolean-like values (true/false, yes/no, on/off, enabled/disabled, 1/0) as booleans.
    - Detect “semantic columns”: A column is semantic if either:
        + the column name suggests a semantic category (examples: status, state, health, severity, result,
            outcome, action, enabled, disabled, mode, presence, compliance, risk, priority), or
        + the column has low cardinality (e.g., ≤ 12 distinct values in the displayed set) and values resemble
            enums/booleans.
    - Render with indicator + label: For semantic columns, display values as:
        "<indicator> <Title Case Label>"
        Use a consistent indicator scheme (only when meaning is clear):

            online|good|healthy|allowed|success|active|enabled|present → 🟢
            caution|warning|degraded|partial|throttled → 🟡
            bad|error|failed|critical|blocked|denied|unhealthy → 🔴
            inactive|offline|down|disabled|absent → ⚫
            unknown|pending|unrecognized|null|empty → ⚪

    - Fallback safely: If semantics cannot be inferred without guessing, Title Case the raw value without an
        icon (or use ⚪ Unknown for null/empty). The assistant MUST NOT invent meanings.

Humanized column names: Column headers MUST be Title Case with spaces (e.g. maintenance_mode → Maintenance Mode)

Strong preferences (SHOULD)
* Prefer ordering by relevance (e.g., highest severity first, most recent first, top N by count).
* For repeated long strings (FQDNs, record names), consider truncation only if it improves readability and
    still answers the question.

name: infoblox-portal_get_table_page
description: Fetch one page of a stored table's data (app-only; see show_table).

name: infoblox-portal_export_table_data
description: Export every row of a stored table as CSV or JSON text (app-only; see show_table).

name: infoblox-portal_user_action
description:
Handle A2UI user-action events.

The A2UI client calls this tool when a user interacts with an
action-bearing component (e.g. a form submit button).  Routing
is based on the ``name`` argument.

name: infoblox-portal_app_ping
description:
Acknowledge a probe from an MCP App shell.

A multiplexing gateway renames this server's tools with a prefix, but an
app only knows the bare names. Calling this under each candidate prefix
finds the one that resolves *before* any action is dispatched, so a wrong
guess costs a no-op instead of a replayed mutation.  Reads and writes
nothing.

name: infoblox-portal_get_dashboard
description: Re-read a dashboard's surface, or report that it has not changed (app-only).

name: infoblox-portal_submit_approval
description: Submit field values to approve a pending action.

name: infoblox-portal_deny_approval
description: Deny a pending approval request.

name: infoblox-portal_always_allow_approval
description: Approve and grant always-allow delegation for this action.

name: infoblox-portal_read_resource
description:
Read a resource by its URI.

For static resources, provide the exact URI. For templated
resources, provide the URI with template parameters filled in.

Returns the resource content as a string. Binary content is
base64-encoded.

name: iq-actions_get_action
description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific action by its ID. Shows complete action details including status, priority, timestamps, and associated information.

name: iq-actions_list_actions
description: List and search actions for your account. Shows action summaries including title, status, priority, and last activity. Supports keyword search (query), filtering by status, priority, type, and creation-date range, plus sorting and pagination. Every parameter is optional, and the filters are combined with AND. With no created_after or created_before, results are limited to actions created in the last 30 days; to search further back, set created_after explicitly (giving either date turns the 30-day default off).

name: iq-actions_list_action_states
description: List the lifecycle states an action can be in for your account, with each state's key, label and category (open or closed). Use the key as status_key in list_actions and update_action.

name: iq-actions_list_allowed_transitions
description: List the states an action can be moved into right now, given the state it is in. Use a returned key as status_key in update_action.

name: iq-actions_update_action
description: Move an existing action to another lifecycle state by status_key, optionally recording a reason. Use list_allowed_transitions to see which states this action can move to now, or list_action_states for every key in your account.
